(Studio: Brian Williams) Report introduced.  

(Capitol: Tom Costello) The administration’s push for approval of its 700-billion dollar plan to prevent a financial collapse featured; scenes shown of Treasury Secretary Henry Paulson and Federal Reserve Board chairman Ben Bernanke before Congress; details given of the sticking points. [At the U.N., President BUSH – says we will act in the urgent time frame required.] [PAULSON&nbsp- says this is all about the American taxpayer; says we need oversight.] [Senators Christopher DODD†, Richard SHELBY†- offer views on the plan.] [BERNANKE – outlines consequences if credit markets are not functioning.] [Speaker of the House Nancy PELOSI – objects to “golden parachutes” for CEOs.]  

(Studio: Brian Williams) Report introduced.  

(Chicago: Kevin Tibbles) The reaction on Main Street over the plan to bail out the financial industry featured. [Lost job and house Travis SOKOP‡, Michigan resident Jane LEW†, Santa Monica resident Maia MOORE†, 63-year-old Susan PROVENCAL‡- express views.] [National Foundation for Credit Counseling Gail CUNNINGHAM†- says consumers feel out of the loop.] [Via his FedUpUSA Website, Karl DENNINGER††- speaks against the plan.]

(Studio: Brian Williams) Report introduced.   (New York: Carl Quintanilla) Where presidential candidates Senators John McCain and Barack Obama stand on the housing crisis examined; statistics on foreclosures cited; details given of each candidate’s proposals. [Detroit homeowner Richard MAGSELLA‡- comments.] [McCAIN – speaks against abusive lending practices.] [OBAMA – supports a tax credit for struggling homeowners.] [Small business owner Sirena MOORE††- says this credit crunch is like crushing your dream.] [Strategas Research Partners Dan CLIFTON†- notes the vicious cycle that happens when business loans dry up.]

(Studio: Brian Williams) Senator Barack Obama’s new ad that criticizes Senator John McCain for owning 13 cars and for owning foreign cars and the tough week for Senator Joe Biden on the campaign trail noted; scenes shown of Governor Sarah Palin at the U.N. with Afghan President Hamid Karzai.    (Studio: Savannah Guthrie) The McCain campaign’s clash with the media over its coverage of Palin featured; scenes shown of her with Colombian President Alvaro Uribe†† and former Secretary of State Henry Kissinger; details given of the decision to ban reporters from Palin’s meetings. [Washington correspondent John HARWOOD†- says the campaign is trying to protect Palin from making a mistake in an unscripted situation.] [Palin senior advisor Steve BIEGUN†- says her meeting with foreign leaders are not just photo ops.]
